column3: WhatsApp Business inbound message capture as new leads
column4: Utilize Convonite's 'Chat Automations' to create an inbound lead-capture bot. When a new user messages, the bot collects basic info (Name/Email) and fires a webhook to the Go backend, which creates the lead record in Supabase and logs the initial interaction on the timeline.

column3: Manual lead entry for offline events, walk-ins, and IG DM enquiries
column4: We will build a simple, dedicated form within the Admin Portal UI for sales/admin users to quickly input required lead data directly into Supabase.

column3: UTM parameter capture on every form for source attribution
column4: We will implement standard URL parsers on all Next.js form endpoints to capture and store the UTM parameters alongside the lead record in Supabase.

column3: API endpoint to ingest leads from any third-party source
column4: A robust and documented API endpoint within the dedicated Go backend will accept standardized JSON payloads, enabling other systems (e.g., event tools, external partners) to push leads.

column3: QR code-based lead capture at online events
column4: This feature will leverage the existing Next.js form implementation and will simply link a QR code to that landing page URL.

column3: Central contact and lead database with custom fields specific to SBM with segregation for batches, program and batch
column4: Supabase PostgreSQL will serve as the central, relational database, utilizing custom table schemas to house contact data and manage the segregation of users by program and specific batch (cohort). This establishes the single source of truth.

column3: Automatic deduplication on email and phone number
column4: Deduplication is handled natively by setting unique constraints on the email and phone number fields within the Supabase PostgreSQL database schema.

column3: Tagging and labelling system
column4: We will implement tagging and labeling using a JSONB column on the contact record in Supabase, allowing for flexible, non-schema-enforced metadata. The Admin UI will provide a user interface for managing and applying these tags.

column3: Lead source attribution (channel, campaign, ad set)
column4: Next.js frontend passes captured UTM parameters and Meta identifiers (fbp/fbc) to the Go backend, which permanently maps the source, medium, and campaign data to the user's Supabase profile for accurate downstream ROI reporting.

column3: Do-not-contact list and unsubscribe tracking
column4: A dedicated boolean flag (e.g., is_unsubscribed) is maintained on the contact record. The Go backend will check this flag before any communication is initiated. The flag will be updated via webhooks from communication tools (Resend, Convonite) or from the user management interface.

column3: Consent capture for DPDP Act compliance
column4: We will capture and log explicit consent and its timestamp during the form submission process (Next.js) or via API ingestion, storing a boolean has_consent flag on the lead record to ensure regulatory compliance.

column3: Lead scoring (demographic plus behavioural signals)
column4: We will implement basic, rules-based lead scoring logic in the Go backend. This engine combines demographic data with early behavioral signals (e.g., website activity) to calculate and store a score on the contact record, providing a quick signal of lead quality.

column3: Machine-learning-based lead scoring trained on historical conversion data
column4: Deferred. While historical Zoho data is being migrated (1.08), building and tuning a bespoke Machine Learning pipeline is a dedicated data science effort outside the scope of the June launch. Focus for V1 is on rules-based lead prioritization.

column3: Data enrichment to auto-fill missing fields where possible
column4: Go backend implements a deterministic matching engine (validating by email or phone) for all inbound leads. If an existing profile is found, the system automatically enriches it by appending the new inbound source (e.g., IG DM, Webinar) to the profile's JSONB tags array. This ensures a unified Customer 360 view of multi-channel engagement without generating duplicate records.

column3: Bucketing by program interest, geography, and lifecycle stage
column4: We will use specific columns in the Supabase contact table (e.g., program_interest, geography, lifecycle_stage) to enable comprehensive segmentation. The Admin UI will provide robust filtering and export capabilities based on these fields.

column3: Standard lifecycle stages: Inquiry, Engaged, Registered, Active, Completed, Renewal Prospect, Lost
column4: These standardized values will be defined and enforced by the Go backend and represented as an ENUM in the Supabase schema to ensure data integrity and consistent application across all touchpoints.

column3: Rules-based automated movement between stages based on actions or time triggers
column4: Automated movement is handled by Supabase Edge Functions. These functions are configured to listen for key database events (e.g., successful payment, program completion) and instantly update the lifecycle_stage field on the corresponding contact record. This maintains real-time user status.

column3: Email campaign builder with rich media templates and scheduling, can it also be made compatible with Canva like platforms
column4: We will build a Template-Based Broadcast Module in the Next.js Admin Portal. Marketing can select from branded React Email templates and insert custom text/images (hosted on Supabase Storage). All emails, including mass blasts to leads, will be deployed via Resend Broadcasts.
column7: Need details on emails to design templates

column3: WhatsApp Business API integration for broadcasts, automated journeys, and one-to-one conversations
column4: Integration will be executed through Convonite. The Go backend will manage API connectivity for broadcasts (handling batching and throttling) and trigger automated sequences via Supabase Edge Functions. One-to-one conversations will be managed through Convonite’s native Messages interface; the CRM will capture and log major interaction events (e.g., Lead Created, Opt-in/Opt-out) to maintain a clean operational history without database bloat.

column3: SMS gateway integration as a third channel
column4: Deferred. Architecture supports future integration of a commercial SMS Gateway API, but the June launch will prioritize automated WhatsApp (Convonite) and Email (Resend) channels.

column3: Unified inbox showing email, WhatsApp, SMS, and call logs against each contact
column4: The CRM serves as a Communication Activity Log. WhatsApp history is accessed via direct deep-links to Convonite. Email history is tracked as 'Sent' events via Resend. For calls, the UI provides native tel: links; upon clicking, a modal allows for Manual Call Logging (outcome and notes). These manual logs are then standardized and displayed alongside automated message events to provide a complete communication history without the complexity of a VoIP integration. SMS is currently deferred to the Future phase.

column3: Click-to-call from contact records with call logging
column4: The UI will provide native tel: links for immediate click-to-call functionality via the admin's device (phone/laptop). Manual Call Logging will be implemented: upon clicking the link, a brief pop-up will allow the team member to quickly log the call outcome (e.g., Interested, Busy, No Answer) and add notes. Automated Call Recording/VoIP integration (via Twilio) is deferred to the Future phase as it requires a separate telephony subscription and significant architectural overhead.

column3: Automated pre-program communication sequences (welcome, prep material, reminders)
column4: These sequences will be managed by utilizing the features of the integrated communication tools (Resend for email and Convonite for WhatsApp). The sequences will be automatically triggered by lifecycle stage updates or batch assignment events managed by Supabase Edge Functions and Vercel Cron jobs.

column3: In-app and push notifications (if a customer-facing app or portal is built)
column4: Supabase Edge Functions will trigger Expo Push Notifications as the primary nudge, falling back to Convonite if push fails.

column3: Multi-language template management- not critical at the current juncture
column4: This feature will be deferred. It involves complex localization logic within the template management system and is not required for the initial launch.

column3: Easy to create workflows with drag drop functionality, no coding requirement
column4: Next.js Admin Portal provides a visual rule builder mapping to a 'Trigger → Condition → Action' flow. Workflows are stored flexibly as JSONB in Supabase. The Go backend acts as the execution engine, evaluating database events against these rules in real-time and leveraging Redis (Asynq) to accurately handle time-delayed or scheduled actions.

column3: Drip email and WhatsApp sequences with branching logic
column4: Go backend manages sequencing state in Supabase. Triggers logic-based messages via Resend and Convonite based on real-time user actions.

column3: A/B testing for email subject lines, body, and send time
column4: A/B testing logic to be implemented via Go backend comparing Resend/Convonite webhooks for conversion rates once core systems are stable.

column3: Trigger-based automations (for example: lead from Meta plus program X, send WhatsApp and assign to rep Y)
column4: Go backend processes external triggers (e.g., Meta Leads) to automate internal rep assignments and multi-channel responses based on database rules.

column3: Personalised content blocks based on user behaviour
column4: Go backend fetches user data (name, batch, link) from Supabase and injects it directly into React Email or Convonite Template Variables.

column4: Strategic future expansion. Architecture is 'AI-Ready' to support a bespoke assistant for lead qualification and FAQs once core operational data is centralized.

column3: Sentiment analysis on inbound WhatsApp and email messages
column4: Deferred feature to analyze lead and student sentiment via LLMs. Planned for implementation once communication volumes reach a statistically significant level.

column3: Renewal communication sequences (email plus WhatsApp)

column3: Renewal status against each contact

column3: Customer lifetime value (CLV) tracking
column4: We will implement a standard SQL function within Supabase to calculate the CLV for each contact based on their historical payment data. This calculated value will be exposed in the Customer 360 View and used for reporting.

column3: Churn risk scoring
column4: Deferred. Advanced behavioral analysis and risk scoring logic will be developed in a future iteration to prioritize core operational analytics and actual churn tracking (11.12) for V1.

column3: Upsell and cross-sell recommendations based on past programs
column4: Deferred. Automated programmatic recommendation logic is designated as a future expansion.

column3: Win-back campaigns for lapsed customers
column4: The Go backend will automatically segment 'Lapsed' customers in Supabase and trigger a specialized Resend Broadcast or Convonite sequence.

column3: Loyalty and referral program management
column4: This is deferred for later consideration. It is a full-scale, dedicated program that involves specialized features like unique referral link generation, commission tracking, and payout logic, which is out of scope for the initial CRM Core Engine build.

column3: Unified contact timeline showing every email, message, call, registration, payment, and attendance event
column4: A centralized React timeline aggregating Operational System Events (Payments, Cohort Assignments) and Communication Milestones. This includes automated email/WhatsApp timestamps and detailed Manual Call Logs.

column3: Program and payment history
column4: The Customer 360 View will directly query the Supabase contact, registration, and payment tables. This history is surfaced in a dedicated, easy-to-read section on the contact’s profile, providing an immediate and comprehensive overview of their transactional relationship.

column3: Meta Lead Ads instant sync into CRM
column4: Go backend implements a webhook listener for Meta Lead Ads to automatically ingest leads into Supabase and trigger immediate notification and welcome workflows.

column4: Custom logic maps specific CRM milestones (Lead, Registration, Payment) to Meta's standard event schema, ensuring 1:1 data alignment across the Pixel and CAPI.

column3: Meta Conversions API setup to send funnel events back for ad optimisation

column3: Ad spend versus revenue dashboards

column4: Deferred. Probabilistic revenue forecasting based on historical funnel velocity. Focus for now is on real-time descriptive analytics.
